ruling.recommended_action: Close the case with no refund; no driver action needed (traffic reason on record, no violation under RD-4).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 18.0 km against an optimal 13.9 km (+4.1 km, +30%) [F1], over one off-route segment at 14:29–14:38 that added 3.73 km [F3], so the RD-1 tolerance of 1 km is exceeded and the excess distance fare on record is $5.78 (4.10 km × $1.4102/km) [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Before that segment began, the driver sent a chat at 14:26 asking "Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Lavender Street?" [F7], and the rider answered at 14:26 "可以，走 Lavender Street 吧。" — an agreement to a specific named road, Lavender Street, sent before the segment started at 14:29 [F8][F9]. Lavender Street is among the roads actually driven on the segment (JALAN BAHAGIA → KIM KEAT ROAD → BALESTIER ROAD → LAVENDER STREET → …) [F3], so the agreed road ties to the segment and the rider's prior, in-scope agreement under RD-5 makes the segment non-refundable [RD-5].

This is not a rider-named stop: no stop was named or measured, so RD-3 does not apply — the exemption rests on RD-5 consent alone [F8][F3][RD-3][RD-5]. The record also shows a traffic reason on the replaced stretch (Central Expressway, band 2, 10–19 km/h, 14:12–14:38), so no driver violation is recorded [F11][RD-4].

With segment F3 exempt, the refundable distance is 4.10 km − 3.73 km = 0.37 km, which is within the 1 km tolerance: (4.10 km − 3.73 km) = 0.37 km ≤ 1 km, so no refund is due [F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2]. The rider's doubt about whether the car took the road she agreed to is answered by the record: Lavender Street was in fact driven, and her own message [F8] agreed to exactly that road [F3][RD-5]. The rider's refund-fraud flag [F16] only raises any decision threshold; it does not decide this case [TH-3].
